evals.name: Writes ADR with alternatives and consequences
evals.prompt: We decided to use Redis for our session store instead of database-backed sessions. Document this decision.
evals.expected_output: The model should write a full ADR including context, decision, alternatives considered with pros/cons, and consequences - not just a one-line note.
assertions: The output follows ADR format with Status, Context, Decision, and Consequences sections.
The output includes alternatives considered (e.g., database sessions, in-memory, Memcached) with explicit pros and cons for each.
The output describes consequences (both positive and negative) of the decision.
The output stores the ADR in docs/decisions/ with sequential numbering.

evals.name: Documents why not what in code comments
evals.expected_output: The model should add comments explaining why the 50 percent threshold exists and why the logic works this way, not just restate what the code does.
assertions: The output adds comments explaining WHY the 50 percent threshold triggers manager approval, not just that it does.
The output does NOT add comments that restate the code (e.g., check if amount is more than half the total).
The output documents non-obvious business rules or constraints the code implements.
The output avoids commenting self-explanatory lines.
